speaker: Doctor
text: I notice the infant is presenting with bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance. Can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if the baby has passed any meconium in the first 48 hours of life?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the newborn pass meconium within the first 48 hours of life, and has an abdominal X-ray been performed to check for bowel dilation or air-fluid levels? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The abdominal X-ray shows a 'double bubble' sign indicative of duodenal atresia.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The previous diagnosis of gastroenteritis is incorrect given the bilious nature of the vomiting, which indicates an intestinal obstruction distal to the ampulla of Vater. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The abdominal X-ray shows a 'double bubble' sign indicative of duodenal atresia.

speaker: Doctor
text: The 'double bubble' sign on the abdominal X-ray is pathognomonic for duodenal atresia, confirming an intestinal obstruction. DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal atresia
